item.title: Philadelphia police ID man in "Chucky-style" mask as Zymire Hughes
item.description: Police have identified the suspect wanted for terrorizing people near Philadelphia City Hall last week while wearing a "Chucky-style" mask.

item.title: Chaplain testifies Lindsay Clancy said "I am so glad my children are safe" after murders
item.description: Sheila Cavanaugh, a chaplain at Brigham and Women's Hospital in Boston, testified on Day 17 of Lindsay Clancy's murder trial. CBS News' Meg Oliver has more details.

item.title: Pentagon officials considering firing Stars and Stripes publisher, sources say
item.description: Max Lederer, who has served as the publisher of Stars and Stripes for 19 years, this week announced to colleagues his decision to retire on Sept. 30, citing fundamental differences with the Trump administration.

item.title: Drug mix-up at Nashville hospital causes complications in 4 patients
item.description: Four patients at Ascension Saint Thomas Midtown received incorrect medications last week, CBS affiliate WTVF reported.

item.title: Pentagon considering firing longtime Stars and Stripes publisher, sources say
item.description: Pentagon officials have discussed firing Max Lederer, the 19-year publisher of Stars and Stripes, before his scheduled retirement at the end of September, U.S. officials tell CBS News. CBS News senior national security correspondent Charlie D'Agata has the latest.

item.title: New U.S. sanctions target cocaine smuggling network in Ecuador
item.description: The U.S. on Thursday imposed fresh sanctions on 15 individuals and entities based in Ecuador for their roles in an alleged maritime cocaine trafficking operation.

item.title: U.S. using stealth operation to move oil through Strait of Hormuz, sources say
item.description: The U.S. is conducting stealth operations to transport oil through the Strait of Hormuz, sources tell CBS News. The development was first reported by Axios. CBS News' Charlie D'Agata has more.

item.title: Iran dismisses Trump's "economic D-Day" threat as more "failed policies"
item.description: Iran has shrugged off President Trump's threat to hit the Islamic Republic with an "economic D-Day" as a "doubling down on failed policies."

item.title: North Korea launches missiles as Trump seeks Kim Jong Un meeting this year
item.description: North Korea fired a number of short-range ballistic missiles, Seoul's military said Thursday, after President Trump said he would meet again with North Korean dictator Kim Jong Un later this year. CBS News' Nancy Cordes reports.

item.title: Army to nix drone battalion set up to absorb lessons from Ukraine war
item.description: The decision to phase out the Army drone battalion comes amid tension between senior officers who envisioned the unit and the acting chief of staff of the Army.

item.title: Army unit offers soldiers time off to play Grand Theft Auto VI if they reenlist for 2 to 6 years
item.description: A U.S. Army unit is offering a few days off to play Grand Theft Auto VI to those who reenlist and commit to several more years in uniform. CBS News' Eleanor Watson reports.

item.title: What goes into a touchdown end zone celebration dance?
item.description: The NFL is launching a new "celly" campaign to honor the tradition of touchdown celebration dances in the end zone. Jason Allen joins the Houston Texans at their training facility to learn more.

item.title: Clear Eyes eye drops recalled nationwide over contamination risk, FDA says
item.description: The recall affects 15mL bottles of Clear Eyes' Maximum Itchy Eye Relief.

item.title: ICE worked directly with Iran on over 100 deportations, emails reveal
item.description: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officials worked closely with Iran to deport Iranian migrants, including asylum seekers, newly released emails reveal. CBS News' Camilo Montoya-Galvez has more information.

item.title: Huge Russian bombardment kills at least 16 in Ukraine
item.description: At least 16 were killed and dozens were injured in Russia's latest attack on Ukraine's capital city. CBS News' Aidan Stretch has more from Kyiv.

item.title: FTC says "personalized pricing" based on consumer data could violate law
item.description: The FTC warned businesses against changing prices based on their analysis of a customer's personal data, which could violate consumer law.

item.title: The fight to protect Big Bend, one of America's last wild places
item.description: Months after Congress approved billions for infrastructure across one of the least-trafficked stretches of the southern border, bulldozers arrived at Big Bend National Park, West Texas's wild crown jewel.

item.title: Police hunt for woman suspected of killing cop husband in Massachusetts
item.description: A manhunt is underway in Massachusetts as law enforcement teams search for a woman suspected of killing her husband, who worked as a police officer. CBS News' Lilia Luciano has more on this story.

item.title: ICE, Iran quietly worked together on deporting Iranians to Iran, emails show
item.description: U.S. immigration officials worked with Iran to deport more than 100 Iranians to Iran in 2025, newly released emails show, revealing a working relationship between them despite tensions mounting at the time.

item.title: U.S. designates American citizen held by China as wrongfully detained
item.description: Min Zin is the second American academic to be designated as wrongfully detained in recent months.

item.title: FBI seizes Swalwell's devices, executes warrants in sexual misconduct probe
item.description: FBI agents executed search warrants targeting former Democratic Rep. Eric Swalwell and seized his electronic devices, two sources told CBS News.

item.title: ICE coordinated with Iran on over 100 deportations, new emails reveal
item.description: New emails show that despite the ongoing U.S. war with Iran, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement worked with Iranian authorities to deport more than 100 Iranian migrants, including asylum seekers. The Department of Homeland Security denies allegations that ICE shared confidential asylum information with the Iranian regime. CBS News' Camilo Montoya-Galvez reports.

item.title: FBI seizes Eric Swalwell's electronic devices in sexual misconduct investigation
item.description: The FBI seized electronic devices belonging to former Democratic Rep. Eric Swalwell as part of an investigation into sexual misconduct claims. CBS News' Jake Rosen explains what we know.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy murder trial closing arguments expected early next week
item.description: Testimony at Lindsay Clancy's trial ended early Thursday as closing arguments are expected next week.

item.title: What to do if you see a giant, invasive spider popping up in multiple states
item.description: The Great Smoky Mountains National Park told visitors Tuesday that invasive Joro spiders "may be hanging in a web near you."

item.title: Bond market sell-off threatens to drive up loan costs
item.description: The yield on the 30-year Treasury this week hit its highest level since 2007, a rise that could put upward pressure on borrowing costs.

item.title: Democrats narrow 2028 convention finalists to 3 cities
item.description: The Democratic National Committee is on the hunt for the best host city for the 2028 Democratic convention.

item.title: Walmart says it is using $2.9 billion in tariff refunds to lower prices
item.description: The company told CBS News it will direct the refunds toward groceries and general merchandise.

item.title: North Korea launches missiles as Trump seeks to rekindle nuclear talks
item.description: Hours after Trump said he expects to hold new talks with Kim Jong Un, South Korea and Japan said several short-range missiles were launched by the North.

item.title: Army unit offers 4-day pass to play Grand Theft Auto as reenlistment incentive
item.description: Eligible soldiers must reenlist for a minimum of two years and up to six years.
